scope: Login-shell PATH hydration at launch for provider resolution (macOS, Linux; Windows registry PATH), scoped to providers so the packaged runtime keeps its system-only PATH
A binary path override per provider in Settings and a --version sanity run on whatever is resolved
A tested-with version range per SDK pin with a warning card outside it
The two platform packages removed from the packaged app; the SDKs given the resolved executable; rehearsals for no tool, a signed-out tool, a shim, and a Finder launch on a clean account

Outside the tested range the provider card warns and names the range; inside it, nothing
Barkdown.app builds at about half its size and a chat runs through the user's tool; without one the install card shows; signed out, the login card shows

truthReview: 2026-10-01: opened. Decision and analysis in the paper The CLI Is Already There (guerrilla.barkpark.cloud/papers/the-cli-is-already-there), linked from C086. Nothing delivered yet. S1 delivered 2026-10-01: shell-environment.js probes the login shell with a bounded time per candidate, merges its PATH ahead of the inherited one, falls back to launchctl (macOS) or the registry (Windows), and feeds provider runs, the sign-in worker, owned workers and the terminal; the main process PATH stays as launched. Unit cases: merge order, a hung shell skipped within budget, a shell that rejects -ilc, launchctl and registry fallbacks, parsers, the singleton. Live: an Electron app launched with the system PATH and a fixture login shell finds a fixture Claude Code and reports signed in, with its own PATH unchanged. One Mac; fixtures, not a real shell. S2 delivered 2026-10-01: provider-tools.js resolves the tool (Settings path first, then the login-shell PATH), runs --version once within a bounded time and accepts only a file that names itself; an impostor, a broken, a hanging, a missing or a relative path each give a plain reason; the sign-in worker follows the chosen path; Settings shows a Tool field per provider. Unit: resolution, sanity run, cache, override. Live: five checks on fixtures. Visual run approved for the new field. Seen on this Mac: another application's bundled claude on the PATH, the wrong-binary case the sanity run exists for. S3 delivered 2026-10-01: scripts/provider-versions.mjs stamps the tool versions the pinned SDKs carry (Claude Code 2.1.276, codex 0.155.0) into main/provider-versions.json, and the unit test fails on an SDK bump without a new stamp; after the --version check the installed version is placed against the stamp: same or a newer minor is silent, older than tested or a different major warns and names the tested version; a tool that is not found gets its install link and login command, opened outside the window. Live: six checks on fixtures (an older tool warns, a different major warns, a current one is silent; Settings shows the warning). Visual run approved.
